searchText: I am also curious about this. If this was done, the only thing the system would have to do is invoke it in each block, before processing txs, to store the root. Why was this path not chosen? Relevant precursor: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-210 i'm open to just enshrining bytecode and i also dont have the bandwidth to make that update before we would want to be in a position to have the EIP final in clients if someone wants to make a pass at it, they are welcome to we would likely want to engage a process of formal verification/auditing of any bytecode we deploy and it is not clear to me if we can move quickly enough on this front to ship this EIP without delaying Cancun yeah, i only skimmed your back and forth here w/ lightclient but a big reason is to support a stateless client paradigm refilled tests with new Cancun names https://github.com/ethereum/tests/pull/1224 It's a pretty tiny contract. I'll take a stab at it awesome! even if we don't have bytecode by tomorrow, let's discuss on ACDE tomorrow I don't normally write solidity, so am a bit rusty. Here's a first draft, which does compile, and as far as I can tell does what it should: https://gist.github.com/holiman/83500097c6497336950817e869082c18 . The contract can be made both smaller and simpler if we have a separate `function` to retrieve values, e.g. callers can invoke`get(uint) returns hash`, but that does not match with the current pseudocode in the eip, hence why I had to mess about with calldata assembly. looks great! thanks for doing this 🙂 will chat about best way forward on call tomorrow

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
I don't normally write solidity, so am a bit rusty. Here's a first draft, which does compile, and as far as I can tell does what it should: https://gist.github.com/holiman/83500097c6497336950817e869082c18 . 
The contract can be made both smaller and simpler if we have a separate `function` to retrieve values, e.g. callers can invoke`get(uint) returns hash`, but that does not match with the current pseudocode in the eip, hence why I had to mess about with calldata assembly.
